lore_anchors.definition: One of the four identical copies sharing the same Zuowandao face; only “Old Four” is the true Heart-Element.
A classic Chinese tile-based game; in this novel, its set structure of four identical Winds and Dragons is weaponized as a system of identity deception.
The Way of Sitting in Forgetfulness; a secret society of liars who weaponize confusion and treat identity as a performance piece.
A rare human constitution that makes the bearer a living alchemical ingredient; the source of Li Huowang’s hallucinations and his value to the world.
The highest-ranked inner circle of the Zuowandao; their appearance signals an escalation in the enemy’s threat level.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why are there four Bei Fengs?
cultural_notes_faq.a: In the Zuowandao, a single public “color” identity like Bei Feng is shared by four members who each play the same role in shifts, making it impossible for outsiders to track them.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What does the mahjong metaphor mean?
cultural_notes_faq.a: A mahjong set contains four identical copies of each wind tile. The Zuowandao use this logic to multiply a single persona, turning social identity into a game of concealment.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Was Bei Feng lying about being a fake?
cultural_notes_faq.a: No. Zhuge Yuan confirmed he is not a Heart-Element. The real target is “Old Four,” one of the other three Bei Feng copies.
